title: Potty Training: Readiness Over Age
hook: There's no magic age to potty train. Readiness signs matter far more — and a calm, child-led, pressure-free approach beats pushing a child who isn't ready yet.
key_points: Look for readiness signs, not a calendar date: staying dry a couple of hours, noticing the urge, and following simple instructions.
Children also need the motor skills to get to the potty and pull pants up and down, plus the words to ask for help.
Go at the child's pace; many kids show real readiness sometime after age 2, but it ranges.
Accidents are a normal part of learning — never punish or shame, which can backfire and slow progress.
content_html: There's no single right age to start potty training. What matters more is readiness, and the AAP describes several signs to watch for: staying dry for a couple of hours at a time, beginning to sense and signal the urge to go, and being able to understand and follow simple instructions. Readiness shows up at different ages for different children — physical readiness can appear well before a child is cognitively or emotionally ready.
extra_html: A child also needs the practical pieces in place: the motor skills to get to the potty and manage their clothes, and enough language to ask for help. Because readiness arrives on each child's own timeline, a relaxed, child-led approach works better than pushing. Accidents are an expected part of learning, not a failure — the goal is patience, not pressure, and shaming or punishing can slow things down. This is general guidance; if you have concerns about your child's progress or readiness, talk to your pediatrician.

related.title: Why Toddlers Have Tantrums
related.hook: Tantrums are a normal part of toddler development — big feelings hitting a brain that can't yet manage them or fully put them into words.

related.title: Positive Discipline: Teaching, Not Punishing
related.hook: Discipline means teaching, not hurting. The AAP's most effective tools are calm consistency, catching good behavior, and clear consequences — and it advises against spanking and harsh words.

flashcards.prompt: What's the best guide to when a child is ready for potty training?

choices.text: Readiness signs like staying dry a while and sensing the urge
Reaching a specific birthday, the same for every child
Whichever date is most convenient for the parents' schedule

flashcards.explanation_html: Readiness varies by child. The AAP emphasizes physical, cognitive, and motor signs over a set age, with readiness often appearing sometime after age two.

flashcards.prompt: How should you handle the inevitable accidents during potty training?
flashcards.back_html: Treat them as a normal part of learning — stay calm and supportive. Punishing or shaming a child can backfire and make training harder.
